title: Cross-Model Serviceability Index and Rapid Recon Kit
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Build a lightweight, repeatable index and toolkit that quantifies 'serviceability' for candidate LLMs across Redwood deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). The index will combine measurable signals (latency dispersion, memory footprint by quantization level, tokenizer mismatch rate, kernel affinity score, cold-start variance, per-region availability) into a single score that product, sourcing, and sales can use to prioritize onboarding and procurement decisions. Deliver an automated Rapid Recon Kit (probe harness + synthetic workloads + scoring dashboard) so field teams can run a 2-hour assessment for any new model and get a serviceability recommendation and expected cost/latency envelope.
acceptance_criteria: Index prototype computes a reproducible score for 6 open-source model families and stores results in the model-watch DB
Rapid Recon Kit includes an automated probe harness, synthetic workload generator, and a one-page result summary PDF
Scoring weights are configurable per customer profile (latency-first, cost-first, regulated) and documented
Runbook for invalid tokenizers and quantization failures with automated fallback suggestions
Dashboard with scatterplots: score vs expected cost, regional variance heatmap, and top-3 risk drivers per model
comments: 2025-02-12 — Aisha: Drafted problem statement after sales request: customers want a quick way to know whether a candidate open model will be usable in production with predictable latency and reasonable infra cost. Aim: 2-hour probe + summary.

2025-02-18 — Jun: Prototype probe harness implemented (CPU and single-GPU flows). Early results show 2x latency variance for 8k-context across some quantized variants; need kernel affinity metric from runtime team.

2025-02-20 — Leah: Ran tokenizer mismatch sweep on 12 domain datasets; detected failure modes for several tokenizers that increase effective token length by 10–25% — added "tokenizer-entropy" as a signal.

2025-02-24 — Diego: Integrated cost model that maps token throughput + batch sizing into expected $/1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated. Observed that small-batch latency-first configs make hosted >2x more expensive on some models.

2025-02-27 — Aisha: PM review — propose scoring weights: latency-dispersion 30%, peak-memory 20%, tokenizer-entropy 15%, quant-failure-rate 15%, regional-availability 10%, kernel-affinity 10%. Request: make weights editable in the UI and document three default profiles.

2025-02-28 — Jun: Engineering review — kernel-affinity currently best-effort; accuracy depends on model attention pattern. Flagging risk: some architectures (sparse attention variants) will need manual vetting; added to runbook.

2025-03-01 — Marta: Field feedback — sales wants an executive one-pager that maps score to recommended procurement option (hosted, dedicated, private) and an estimated migration effort (low/med/high). Added this to deliverables.

2025-03-03 — Diego: Ran Rapid Recon on three external candidate models (ModelA-v0.9, ModelB-XL, ModelC-quant32). Summary: ModelA scores 0.72 (recommended hosted canary with quant fallback), ModelB 0.44 (dedicated recommended due to memory/latency variance), ModelC 0.58 (private + quant-tuning suggested). Attached draft PDFs to GH PR.

2025-03-04 — Aisha: Roadblock noted — regulatory checklist missing for private deployments in EU (data residency, KMS requirements). Raised ticket to security: PM-558123 looks related; raising dependency for legal clearance before public rollout.
Next steps: finalize scoring config UI, complete PR for rapid-recon-kit, QA run for additional 6 models, and prepare sales one-pager and technical runbook.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: weighting latency-dispersion favors low-latency apps but penalizes generalist models that exhibit high variance with long-context; to mitigate, profiles will have separate thresholds.
Decision: include both absolute latency (median P50) and dispersion (P95–P50) in the index to capture tail behavior.

Implementation detail: the probe will attempt 4 quantization levels automatically (fp16, int8, q4m, q8_0) and record failures. If quantization fails, record a hard penalty and recommended remediation steps.
Operationalization: results will feed model-watch alerts; if a model's serviceability score drops by >0.15 between runs, trigger 're-eval' and notify sourcing and infra.
Edge case: private air-gapped installs may not support automated quant probe — provide a manual checklist and sample scripts in the kit.
